The RN assigns staff by matching client needs to caregiver qualifications and competency records. Clients may accept or reject any referred caregiver without retaliation.

When a client declines part of the recommended plan or requests a waiver of skilled services, the RN conducts and documents a risk/benefit discussion and obtains a signed, dated form under IC-01 and IC-03.

Only a CNA or CMT may receive delegated nursing tasks. A worker who administers medications must be a CMT, and a worker who performs other delegated nursing functions must also be a CNA. The RN verifies the certification before delegating.

For each delegation, the RN decides whether the task may be safely delegated under COMAR 10.27.11, instructs the worker, confirms the worker can perform the task, records the delegation (task, client, worker, date, instruction, return demonstration), and states when the RN will re-evaluate.
The RN may withdraw a delegation at any time for client safety, and records the withdrawal and the reason.

The RN prepares written worker instructions for each client and reviews them with the assigned caregiver before the first visit. The caregiver signs that the instructions were received and understood.

For Medicaid participants, the RN confirms that caregiver instructions are consistent with the authorized plan of service. Caregivers accept instruction about the plan from the participant or representative, the nurse monitor, a treating physician or nurse practitioner, or MDH, and tell the RN promptly of any instruction that changes the plan.
The agency never assigns a participant's representative as that participant's paid worker. Scheduling staff check the representative designation before a worker is assigned.
The RN supports the participant's role in directing services, including selecting, training, scheduling, setting duties for, and dismissing the worker, and documents these preferences in the plan.

The RN updates the plan of care within 7 calendar days after any reassessment that changes needs, and sends changes to the client, caregiver, and (for Medicaid participants) the case manager or supports planner as required by PC-11.
The QAPI lead audits assessment dates, plan content, and delegation records each quarter under ADM-08.

responsibilities.duty: Performs assessments and reassessments, develops plans of care, assigns staff, delegates and documents nursing tasks, and trains caregivers.
Makes sure a qualified RN is employed, verifies licenses and certifications, and provides resources for timely assessment.
Perform only delegated tasks they are certified and trained for, and report changes in client condition promptly.
Follow written worker instructions, accept instruction as stated in this policy, and report changes in condition or instructions that differ from the plan.
Notify the RN of requests and changes, and track assessment due dates.

documentation: RN license verification
Initial assessment and all reassessments with dates and times
Documentation of 7-day exception reasoning when the 48-hour assessment is not done
Plan of care with all required elements and client/representative acknowledgment
Signed informed consent and waiver forms with risk/benefit discussion
Delegation records and withdrawals
CNA/CMT certification verification
Signed worker instruction acknowledgments
Assessment due-date tracking list
Quarterly QAPI audit results

policies.title: RN Supervision, Supervisory Visits and 24/7 On-Call
policies.applies_to: RN Supervisor, Administrator, on-call staff, scheduling staff, and caregivers
policies.purpose: To make sure the RN supervises caregivers on-site at the intervals required, documents each visit, and that every client and caregiver can reach a responsible person at any hour.
policies.policy: This policy meets COMAR 10.07.05.08B(1)(a)(viii) (Application p.5, item B(1)(a)(viii) — Administration: clinical management, including assessment, plans, delegation, and supervision); the supervision component is addressed here. The RN supervises caregivers on-site at least every 45 days if staff administer medications, at least every 3 months if staff assist with self-administration of medications, and at least every 4 months in all other cases. The RN may visit more often when clinically appropriate. Every supervisory visit is documented. [AGENCY NAME] maintains 24-hour, 7-day-a-week contact: a person responds to calls within 1 hour, every call is entered in an on-call log, and each client receives written on-call procedures and the on-call phone number. Missed or late supervisory visits are reported to the Administrator.

definitions.definition: An on-site visit by the RN to the client's home to observe the caregiver, evaluate care against the plan, and assess the client.
Staff, as a CMT or licensed nurse and under physician orders, give the client's medications.
Staff help a client who takes his or her own medication, for example by reminders, opening containers, or handing the medication.
A qualified person designated to receive and respond to client and caregiver calls outside business hours.
A record of every after-hours call, response time, action taken and follow-up.

procedures: At each assessment and plan update, the RN classifies each client's supervision tier: every 45 days (staff administer medications); every 3 months (staff assist with self-administration); every 4 months (all others). The tier is written on the plan of care and in the supervision tracker.
The supervision tracker lists each client, the tier, last visit date, and next due date. The RN Supervisor updates it within 1 business day after each visit.
Scheduling staff send the RN a due-date list at least 14 days before each visit is due. The RN schedules the visit to fall on or before the due date, not after it.
The RN visits on-site while the caregiver is present, and confirms the client's consent to the visit in advance when possible.

During the visit, the RN observes the caregiver's performance of tasks, checks that care is consistent with the plan of care and worker instructions, reviews medication records and any errors or adverse reactions, and assesses the client's condition, safety, and satisfaction.
If the RN finds that the care plan no longer fits the client, a reassessment is begun under ADM-09 and the plan is revised.

The RN completes a Supervisory Visit Note on the day of the visit, recording date, time, persons present, observations, client comments, any teaching, problems found and the follow-up action. The RN signs and dates it.

The RN may supervise more often than the minimum, such as after a new caregiver starts, a medication error, a complaint, a significant change in condition, or a hospital discharge. The reason for increased frequency is documented.

If a supervisory visit cannot be done by its due date (for example, the client is hospitalized or refuses entry), the RN notifies the Administrator the same business day and documents the reason and the makeup date. The visit is made as soon as possible.
The Administrator reviews a monthly report of all supervisory visits that were missed or late, and requires a corrective action under ADM-08 for any pattern.

[AGENCY NAME] maintains a 24/7 on-call phone number [PHONE]. The Administrator posts an on-call schedule at least 2 weeks ahead naming a primary on-call person and a backup, and the on-call person is a nurse or has immediate access to the RN Supervisor.
The on-call person answers or returns every call within 1 hour. If the call is not answered or returned within 1 hour, the backup is called and the Administrator is told the next business day.

For every call, the on-call person enters in the on-call log the date and time received, caller, client, nature of the issue, advice or action, time of response, and any follow-up needed. The RN Supervisor reviews the log each business day.
Calls about a change in condition or emergency are handled per PC-09. Calls about suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation are handled per ENV-08. Incidents are handled per ENV-09.

At admission, the intake coordinator gives each client written on-call procedures stating the 24/7 phone number, what to expect when calling, and the RN care supervisor's name and contact. The client or representative signs for receipt.
Caregivers receive the on-call procedures at orientation and a wallet card or schedule with the number.
The QAPI lead audits on-call response time and the percentage of supervisory visits completed on time each quarter.

responsibilities.duty: Sets the supervision tier, completes and documents supervisory visits on time, reviews the on-call log daily.
Receives reports of missed or late visits, maintains on-call coverage, and ensures corrective action.
Respond within 1 hour and record every call in the on-call log.
Maintain the supervision tracker and send due-date lists.
Provide on-call procedures and number to each client at admission.

documentation: Supervision tier noted on plan of care
Supervision tracker with last and next due dates
Supervisory Visit Notes signed and dated
Reports of missed or late visits to the Administrator and corrective actions
On-call schedule
On-call log with response times
Signed receipt of written on-call procedures and phone number
Quarterly QAPI audit of supervision timeliness and on-call response

policies.title: Licensure, Service Area, Advertising and Changes Affecting the License
policies.applies_to: Owners, Administrator, governing authority, and staff involved in marketing or intake
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] obtains and keeps its Maryland Residential Service Agency license, operates only within the scope of that license, advertises accurately, and gives the State the required notice of changes.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] is a Residential Service Agency, an entity that employs or contracts with workers to provide at least one home health care service to an unrelated sick or disabled person at home, and operates under a license issued by the Maryland Department of Health, Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ). The license is valid for 3 years. Renewal requires the renewal fee, any substantively changed policies (including those on complaints and client evaluation), valid licenses and certificates for current employees, and the annual data collection survey. The person who controls [AGENCY NAME]'s pay and employment practices has read the RSA-PCA Guidance Document and submitted the online RSA worker-classification certification form (Health-General §19-4A-11), which is a condition of obtaining and keeping the license. [AGENCY NAME] gives written notice 45 days in advance of closure, change of ownership, location, name or tax ID, or sale, to OHCQ and to Maryland Medicaid, including how clients will be informed and a transition plan. A new owner must apply for a new license. [AGENCY NAME] advertises only services listed on its license and serves only within its service area.

definitions.definition: An agency that employs or contracts with workers to provide at least one home health care service to an unrelated sick or disabled person at home.
The owner or board that is legally responsible for the agency and that meets at least annually with management.
A limited license OHCQ may issue while an agency corrects deficiencies or completes requirements.
The online RSA certification by the person who controls pay and employment practices, filed after reading the RSA-PCA Guidance Document.
The Maryland jurisdictions in which [AGENCY NAME] has adequate staff and supervision to deliver services.

procedures: Before applying for or renewing the license, the Administrator confirms that every applicant or owner is 21 or older, and prepares disclosures of owners holding 25% or more, any prior license actions, and any criminal charges and Medicare/Medicaid violations.
The Administrator prepares the application package: business plan (1-year budget, populations served, services), the policies and procedures manual, and proof of workers' compensation insurance.

The Administrator confirms with OHCQ the fee due and when it is billed. The regulation provides a $1,000 nonrefundable fee for a 3-year license, and OHCQ's current application states there is no fee to apply. The confirmation is documented in the licensing file.

The person who controls pay and employment practices reads the RSA-PCA Guidance Document and submits the online RSA Certification form, and the confirmation is placed in the licensing file. The certification is reviewed again whenever pay or employment practices change and before each renewal.

The Administrator cooperates with any OHCQ pre-licensure inspection, understands OHCQ may approve with conditions (such as a management firm for up to 24 months or a term under 1 year) or issue a provisional license, and that OHCQ may charge $250 for each additional pre-licensure visit.
The Administrator posts the license in the office, records the effective and expiration dates on the compliance calendar, and sets reminders at 180, 120 and 90 days before expiration.

At least 90 days before expiration, the Administrator begins renewal: reviews policies for substantive changes (especially complaints and client evaluation), verifies licenses and certificates for all current employees, completes the annual OHCQ data collection survey, and prepares the $1,000 renewal fee.

The Administrator defines the service area by jurisdiction in writing, based on caregiver availability and RN supervision capacity. Intake staff do not accept clients outside the service area unless the Administrator approves in writing and RN supervision and 24/7 coverage are confirmed.

Marketing materials, website, social media, directory listings and contracts describe only the services authorized under the license and provided by the agency. Staff do not advertise skilled services, or use clinical titles, that the agency is not licensed and staffed to provide.

Before any new advertisement is published, the Administrator reviews it against the license, the services actually provided, and the advertising provisions of the RSA regulations (confirmed with OHCQ if there is any doubt), and initials the approved copy. Approved copy is kept for 3 years.

The Administrator sends written notice at least 45 days before closure, change of ownership, change of location, change of name, change of tax ID, or sale to OHCQ and to Maryland Medicaid (MDH). The notice states the effective date, how clients will be informed, and the transition plan.

For each Medicaid participant, the notice and transition plan go to the case manager or supports planner and to the participant or representative. The RN Supervisor leads continuity-of-care planning under PC-10 so services are not interrupted.
On a transfer of ownership, the new owner applies for a new license before assuming operation, and Medicaid enrollment is updated through the Medicaid provider enrollment system.

The Administrator reports to OHCQ any changes in the information on the application (owners, administrator, services, address) as OHCQ requires. Any change to the services offered is reviewed by the governing authority before it is made.

The Administrator screens owners and principals against the 24-month look-back events (license suspension or revocation, Medicaid suspension or sanction, disciplinary action, State deficiency citations affecting health and safety, and agreement terminations) and records the result annually under ADM-12.
OHCQ is reachable at 410-402-8040, and its complaint line is 800-492-6005. The Administrator keeps these numbers in the licensing file and in client rights materials.

responsibilities.duty: Approves service area and service changes, and signs off on notices of ownership or location changes.
Maintains the license, completes renewals and the worker-classification certification, approves advertising, and sends required notices.

responsibilities.role: Person controlling pay and employment practices
responsibilities.duty: Completes and maintains the online RSA worker-classification certification.
Use only approved advertising and accept clients only within the service area and scope of the license.
Confirms supervision and on-call capacity before service-area expansion and leads transition planning.

documentation: Copy of RSA license and compliance calendar
Application and renewal packages, with disclosures, business plan, workers' compensation proof, and fee records
Worker-classification certification confirmation
OHCQ correspondence, inspection reports and any conditions
Written service area definition
Approved advertising copy with Administrator initials
45-day notices, transition plans and client notification records
Annual look-back screening record
Governing authority minutes for changes

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
policies.applies_to: Owners, Administrator, compliance officer, billing and scheduling staff, RN Supervisor, caregivers, and contractors
policies.purpose: To prevent, detect and correct fraud, waste and abuse; to keep [AGENCY NAME] eligible as a Medicaid provider; and to meet Maryland Medicaid and federal compliance, audit and wage reporting obligations.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] bills Medicaid only for services that were delivered, documented in ISAS, authorized, and consistent with the plan of service and the provider agreement. To remain a Medicaid provider, [AGENCY NAME] carries no unpaid overpayments and has no conflicts of interest, and its principals are free of the 24-month look-back events: license suspension or revocation, Medicaid suspension or sanction, disciplinary action, State deficiency citations affecting health and safety, and agreement terminations. [AGENCY NAME] cooperates with inspections, reviews and audits, including DPICC audits under PT 13-27. It responds to a plan of correction within 15 calendar days and answers every outreach, because non-responders are suspended after three outreach attempts. Repeat findings within 6 months can bring sanctions. [AGENCY NAME] files the annual personal care aide wage report with the Maryland Department of Labor by September 1 and monitors the federal payment adequacy and rate transparency requirements (42 CFR 441.302(k) and 447.203), including the 80% direct-care compensation standard applicable from July 9, 2030. Federal law on payment suspension for credible allegations of fraud (42 CFR 455.23) and the False Claims Act (31 U.S.C. 3729) apply, and staff may report concerns without retaliation.

definitions.definition: Knowingly submitting or causing a false claim or statement to obtain payment to which the agency is not entitled.
Any payment received that the agency is not entitled to, including payment for undocumented, unauthorized or undelivered services.
A financial or personal interest that could influence, or appear to influence, decisions about client care, referrals, billing or contracting.
An event in the prior 24 months involving the provider or its principals that can affect Medicaid participation, as listed in COMAR 10.09.84.05B.
The Maryland Department of Health's Division of Provider Integrity, Claims and Compliance, which audits RSAs and may withhold payment.
A written response describing how deficiencies found in an audit will be corrected, and by when.

procedures: The Administrator designates a compliance officer in writing (the Administrator unless otherwise assigned) and gives all staff the compliance officer's name and a confidential way to report concerns, including anonymously.

All staff receive compliance training at hire and annually. The training covers accurate time and visit documentation, false claims, kickbacks, conflicts of interest, and how to report concerns. Attendance is recorded in the personnel file.

Billing staff submit claims only when the visit appears in ISAS, matches the schedule and plan of service, and is supported by a caregiver service note. Any claim without these is held and reviewed by the compliance officer.

Caregivers must never falsify clock-in/out, ask another person to clock for them, record time for services not provided, or alter service documentation. Violations result in discipline up to termination and are reported as required.

The compliance officer reviews at least monthly: visits with unusually short or long durations, overlapping visits, ISAS exceptions and manual corrections, and visits during client hospitalization. Findings go into the QAPI process under ADM-08.

On discovery of any overpayment, the compliance officer notifies the Administrator within 2 business days, quantifies the amount, and arranges prompt repayment or correction in the manner the Department requires. No unpaid overpayment is allowed to remain outstanding.

Every owner, principal, officer and manager discloses actual or potential conflicts of interest annually in writing and whenever they arise. The governing authority reviews disclosures and documents how each is managed.
Staff are not allowed to accept payments or gifts in return for referrals or client choice, and agency referrals are made based on client need and choice only.

At least annually, and before each license renewal and Medicaid revalidation, the compliance officer checks each principal and the agency against the 24-month look-back events, records the result, and reports any event to the governing authority within 5 business days.

The Administrator checks the Medicaid exclusion and sanction lists for every employee, contractor and principal at hire and at least monthly thereafter, and removes anyone found on a list from Medicaid-funded work immediately.
The Administrator cooperates with all inspections, reviews and audits, makes records available promptly, and designates one contact for DPICC and Department correspondence.

On receiving a DPICC audit or outreach notice, the Administrator records the date, responds the same business day, and escalates. The agency never allows three outreach attempts to pass without a response.

The compliance officer prepares the plan of correction, with root causes, corrective actions, owners and dates, and submits it within 15 calendar days. If there is a repeat finding within 6 months, the Administrator reports it to the governing authority within 5 business days and reviews the systems that failed.

If the Department notifies [AGENCY NAME] of a payment withhold or suspension, the Administrator contacts legal counsel, preserves all records, and follows the Department's instructions on response and appeal.

When the compliance officer suspects a possible false claim or fraud, the compliance officer preserves records, informs the Administrator and counsel, stops billing for the affected claims, and decides on self-disclosure and repayment. Suspected abuse, neglect, self-neglect or exploitation of a client is reported to the local department of social services immediately under ENV-08.
Reports of incidents and complaints are made within 24 hours of knowledge to the Department, with the written report within 7 calendar days on the Department's form, per ENV-09.

Each year, before September 1, the Administrator files the annual personal care aide wage report with the Maryland Department of Labor, using payroll data reviewed by the compliance officer, and keeps the confirmation.

The Administrator tracks the federal payment adequacy and rate transparency requirements, including the 80% direct-care compensation standard applicable from July 9, 2030. Each year the agency compares direct-care compensation as a share of Medicaid personal assistance revenue and reports the result to the governing authority.
No employee or contractor who reports a concern in good faith is retaliated against. Any retaliation is a disciplinary matter, and the Administrator documents each report and its resolution.
The compliance officer reports compliance activity, audit results, overpayments and corrective actions to the governing authority at least annually, and as events occur for serious matters.

responsibilities.duty: Oversee compliance, review conflict disclosures and look-back screening, and act on repeat findings.
Responds to DPICC and Department outreach, files the wage report, ensures repayments, and answers for the compliance program.
Runs monthly reviews, exclusion checks, training, plans of correction and the confidential reporting channel.
Submit only supported claims and hold questionable claims for review.
Document accurately, never falsify time or records, and report concerns.

policies.title: Medicaid Provider Participation, Enrollment and Cost Survey (CFC/CPAS, PT 76)
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Director of Nursing/Supervising RN, billing and compliance staff, schedulers, and all employees and contractors who deliver or document Medicaid-funded personal assistance
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] enrolls and stays enrolled as a Maryland Medicaid provider (provider type 76) for Community First Choice (CFC) and the Community Personal Assistance Services program (CPAS). The policy also makes sure the agency meets the provider conditions in COMAR 10.09.84.05, 10.09.84.06 and 10.09.20.05, files required reports and surveys on time, and bills only for authorized services.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will provide Medicaid personal assistance only while it is enrolled in MPRIME as provider type 76, holds a current OHCQ RSA license, employs a Registered Nurse, and meets the Medicaid participation conditions in COMAR 10.09.84.05 and 10.09.84.06 (CFC) and COMAR 10.09.20.05 (CPAS). The agency will bill only for services that are preauthorized in the participant's plan of service, delivered consistent with that plan, and within the provider agreement. It will keep its MPRIME record current, including its SDAT ID in good standing and its uploaded RSA license. It will file the annual HCBS Cost Survey on time. The agency will not suspend, terminate, increase or reduce services without Department authorization and consultation with the participant. Services delivered under this policy support the person-centered, home and community-based service requirements of 42 CFR 441.301(c) and 42 CFR 441.710, including the participant's significant role in directing services. This policy has no separate official checklist item. It supports the Medicaid conditions of participation cited above.

definitions.definition: The Maryland Medicaid provider enrollment and revalidation system, which went live October 13, 2026.
The Medicaid provider type under which Residential Service Agencies enroll to deliver personal assistance.
The agency's Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation identification, which must remain in good standing. MPRIME auto-suspends providers that lose good standing.
The annual Home and Community-Based Services Cost Survey issued by the Department. The current survey is due December 31, 2026.
The Medicaid-authorized document that states the personal assistance services, hours and units a participant is approved to receive.

For the 24 months before enrollment or participation, any license suspension or revocation, Medicaid suspension or sanction, disciplinary action, State deficiency citation affecting health and safety, or provider agreement termination involving the provider or its principals.

procedures: The Administrator is the agency's Medicaid compliance lead and keeps a Medicaid Compliance Calendar listing every due date in this policy, with a named owner for each.

If the agency has not yet completed MPRIME enrollment, the Administrator submits a complete PT 76 application as early as possible and no later than December 31, 2026. A complete application filed by that date can be backdated under PT 36-27. The Administrator keeps the submission confirmation in the Medicaid Enrollment File.

Before applying and at each revalidation, the Administrator reviews the agency and each principal for look-back events in the prior 24 months, unpaid Medicaid overpayments and conflicts of interest. The review is signed and dated. If any issue is found, the Administrator consults OLTSS at 410-767-1739 before proceeding.

The Administrator confirms the agency's SDAT ID is in good standing at enrollment and checks it at least quarterly. Any SDAT lapse is corrected the same day it is found, because MPRIME auto-suspends a provider that loses good standing.

The Administrator uploads the current RSA license to MPRIME by March 31, 2027, and uploads each renewed license within 10 days of receiving it. An expired license triggers suspension from April 1, 2027. The Administrator calendars the license expiration date at 180, 90 and 30 days.

The Administrator files the HCBS Cost Survey by December 31, 2026, and each later survey by the date the Department sets. Payment is suspended from January 1, 2027 for non-filers. Billing staff assemble payroll, cost and hours data by November 15, and the Administrator signs and submits the survey and keeps a copy and the submission confirmation.

The agency maintains the RN required by COMAR 10.09.84.06. The Director of Nursing confirms the RN's license is current and that the RN assesses each new participant, helps develop worker instructions, assigns staff and instructs workers (see ADM-09 and ADM-10).

Before accepting a Medicaid referral, intake staff confirm the plan of service, authorized units and the case manager or supports planner contact. Billing staff verify the participant's Medicaid eligibility at the start of each month of service and record the date and result in the participant's billing file.

The agency bills only authorized services at the Medicaid rates in effect. Current published rates are $6.3962 per 15-minute unit for W5519 (CFC) and W5527 (CPAS), $4.2597 per 15 minutes for shared attendant (W5521/W5528), and $329.84 for the daily rate for more than 12 hours per day (W5532). Billing staff check the Department's current rate transmittals before July 1 of each year and whenever a new transmittal is issued. They update billing tables and record the transmittal number.

Claims are generated from visits verified in the state's electronic visit verification system (see PC-08). Billing staff reconcile claims to the plan of service each billing cycle, and the Administrator reviews any variance before submission.
The agency collects the participant's or representative's signature at least monthly verifying services were delivered. The signed verification is filed in the service record (see PC-07 and REC-01).

Workers accept instruction on the plan of service from the participant or representative, the nurse monitor, a treating physician or nurse practitioner, or MDH. Participants keep a significant role in selecting, training, scheduling, setting duties for and dismissing their worker. The participant's representative is never assigned as the worker.

Before assignment, HR staff obtain and file written verification of each worker's qualifications, and criminal history checks are completed for all direct service workers including nurses (see PER-03).

Incidents and complaints involving Medicaid participants are reported to the Department within 24 hours of the agency's knowledge. A written report on the Department's form follows within 7 calendar days. Suspected abuse, neglect, self-neglect or exploitation is reported immediately to the local department of social services (see ENV-08, ENV-09 and REC-02).

The agency does not suspend, terminate, increase or reduce services without Department authorization and consultation with the participant. When services end or change, the Director of Nursing sends a transition plan to the case manager or supports planner and the participant (see PC-10).

The Administrator gives MDH 45 days' written notice before any closure, change of ownership, location, name or tax ID, or sale. The notice states how participants will be informed and includes a transition plan. On a transfer of ownership, the new owner applies for a new RSA license (see ADM-11).

Service documentation, including dates and hours of service, is kept for 6 years from the date of service. The agency cooperates promptly with inspections, reviews and audits by OHCQ, OLTSS, DPICC and other Department reviewers. The Administrator is the single point of contact, and a written plan of correction is submitted by the due date set by the reviewer.

The Administrator reviews compliance with this policy at each quarterly QA meeting (see ADM-08) and reports results to the governing authority at its annual meeting (see ADM-01). Questions are directed to MPRIME at 1-844-463-7768, OLTSS at 410-767-1739, or mdh.cfcprovidersrsas@maryland.gov.

policies.title: Job Descriptions and Educational Qualifications for Employees and Contractors
policies.applies_to: Administrator, human resources staff, supervising RN, and all employees, independent contractors and contractual employees
policies.purpose: To define in writing the duties, education and license or certification required for every position and contracted role at [AGENCY NAME]. This ensures that only qualified individuals are referred to clients and that tasks are assigned only to those authorized to perform them.
policies.policy: This policy meets Application p.5 (Personnel) item B(1)(b)(i), Personnel - Job descriptions and educational qualifications for all employees and contractors, and COMAR 10.07.05.08B(1)(b)(i). [AGENCY NAME] maintains a current written job description for every position and contracted role, including the Administrator, Registered Nurse, Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA), Certified Medication Technician (CMT), personal care aide and scheduler. Each description states the required education, license or certification, reporting line, essential duties and limits of practice. Contractors and contractual employees meet the same qualifications as employees performing the same work. The RN must hold a current Maryland nursing license. Medication administration is performed only by a CMT or licensed staff. Aides who perform delegated nursing tasks must be CNAs. The participant's representative may not be assigned as the participant's worker. No one is referred to a client unless the individual meets the qualifications in the job description.

definitions.definition: A written statement of a position's title, qualifications, duties, supervision and limits of authority, signed by the holder.
A nursing assistant certified in Maryland who may perform nursing tasks delegated by the RN within the scope of that certification.
A certified medication technician authorized in Maryland to administer medications under the delegation and supervision of a licensed nurse.
An individual or agency that provides services to or for the agency under a written agreement rather than as a W-2 employee.
A caregiver who provides non-skilled assistance such as personal care and household support under the RN's plan of service.

procedures: The Administrator, with the Director of Nursing, writes and approves a job description for each position and contracted role. At minimum these are Administrator, Registered Nurse (supervising nurse), CNA, CMT, personal care aide and scheduler. Each uses the agency's standard job description form.

Each job description states: title; required education; required license or certification and the verification source; reporting relationship; essential duties; tasks the role may not perform; and physical and training requirements.

The Administrator job description requires [ADMINISTRATOR QUALIFICATIONS, e.g., degree and years of home care experience as set by the governing authority]. It assigns responsibility for day-to-day operations, regulatory compliance, and the policy review described in ADM-01.

The RN job description requires a current Maryland RN license. It assigns client assessment, plan-of-care development, delegation, instruction of workers, supervisory visits and on-call coverage (see ADM-09 and ADM-10).

The CNA job description requires current certification in good standing. It states that the CNA performs delegated nursing tasks only after RN delegation and instruction. The CMT job description requires current CMT certification. It states that medication administration is performed only by a CMT or licensed staff (see PC-03).

The personal care aide job description states the qualifications set by the agency, training required before referral (see PER-06), and that the aide performs only the tasks in the plan of service and no nursing tasks unless certified and delegated. It states that the aide takes instruction on the plan of service from the participant or representative, nurse monitor, treating physician or NP, or MDH.

The scheduler job description states that the scheduler assigns only workers who are qualified for the client's needs as determined by the RN, and may not assign a participant's representative as the participant's worker.
Before offering any position, HR staff give the applicant the job description. The applicant signs and dates it at hire, and the signed copy goes in the personnel file.

Before offering a position or contract, HR staff verify required education and license or certification from the primary source, such as the Maryland Board of Nursing for nurses and CNAs. The verification is printed or saved, dated and initialed.

For contractors and contractual employees, HR staff include the applicable job description as an attachment to the written agreement. Subcontract agencies must verify their personnel's information and give the agency evidence of that verification (see PER-10).

Before assigning a worker to a client, the scheduler checks the worker's role and credentials against the RN's assignment instructions. If a task requires a CNA or CMT, only a worker with that certification is assigned.

The Director of Nursing reviews job descriptions at least annually and whenever regulations or services change. The Administrator approves revisions, records the revision date, and has affected staff sign the updated description.
The governing authority reviews the job descriptions and qualifications during its annual policy review (see ADM-01).

If an employee's or contractor's license or certification lapses, is restricted or is revoked, the employee is removed from duties requiring that credential immediately. The Administrator documents the action and reports to the Board of Nursing and OHCQ where conduct may be grounds for Board action (see PER-03).

responsibilities.duty: Approves all job descriptions, ensures qualifications are verified before hire or contract, and reports credential problems.
Defines clinical roles and limits, delegates tasks only to qualified staff, and reviews clinical job descriptions annually.
Provide job descriptions to applicants, verify credentials from primary sources, and file signed descriptions.
Assigns only qualified workers consistent with the RN's instructions.
Reviews job descriptions and qualifications at its annual policy review.

policies.title: Caregiver Qualifications, Certified vs. Non-Certified Caregivers and Worker Classification
policies.applies_to: Administrator, supervising RN, schedulers, HR staff, and all caregivers
policies.purpose: To make sure each client receives a caregiver with the correct level of certification for the client's needs, and to document how [AGENCY NAME] classifies its caregivers for pay and employment purposes, as required for RSA licensure.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides a certified caregiver to any client who needs one for activities of daily living (ADLs) or for medication administration. A non-certified caregiver is provided only when the client needs no ADL help, needs ADL help with no predictable adverse health consequences in the supervising nurse's judgment, or has signed a waiver of skilled services (see IC-03). Medication administration is performed only by a CMT or licensed staff, and delegated nursing tasks are performed only by CNAs. The participant's representative is never assigned as the participant's worker. The agency classifies its aides as W-2 employees unless counsel advises otherwise in writing. The person who controls pay and employment practices has read the RSA-PCA Guidance Document and submitted the OHCQ online RSA Certification form, which is a condition of obtaining and keeping the license under Health-General §19-4A-11. The agency follows the federal rules on domestic service employment in 29 CFR Part 552 when it sets pay practices. This policy has no separate official checklist item.

definitions.definition: A caregiver who holds current Maryland certification as a CNA or, for medication administration, a CMT.
A personal care aide who has completed agency training but does not hold CNA or CMT certification.
Activities of daily living such as bathing, dressing, toileting, transferring, mobility and eating.
A written statement signed by the client or representative accepting a non-certified caregiver despite a need identified by the agency (see IC-03).
The online worker-classification certification submitted to OHCQ by the person who controls pay and employment practices after reading the RSA-PCA Guidance Document.

procedures: At intake, the RN assesses the client's need for ADL assistance and medication help (see ADM-06 and ADM-09). The RN records whether the client (a) needs no ADL help, (b) needs ADL help, or (c) needs medication administration.
If the client needs no ADL help, the RN records that a non-certified caregiver may be assigned.

If the client needs ADL help, the RN decides whether any predictable adverse health consequence could result from the assistance. The RN writes this judgment and its basis in the assessment, dated and signed. If there is no predictable adverse consequence, a non-certified caregiver may be assigned.

If the RN finds a predictable adverse health consequence, a certified caregiver is required. The agency assigns a CNA. If none is available, the agency tells the client, offers a waiver of skilled services (see IC-03), or arranges a transition (see PC-10).
Any client who needs medication administration is assigned a CMT or licensed nurse. Non-certified staff do not administer medications (see PC-03 and IC-02).

A non-certified caregiver is assigned to a client with ADL needs and predictable adverse consequences only if the client or representative has signed the waiver of skilled services after the RN explains the risks. The RN files the waiver before the first visit.
The RN writes the caregiver level required into the plan of service and worker instructions. The scheduler assigns only workers at that level or higher.

The RN reassesses the required caregiver level at each supervisory visit and when the client's condition changes (see ADM-10 and PC-09). If the level increases, the RN notifies the scheduler and the client the same day and revises the plan.
The scheduler never assigns the participant's representative as the participant's worker. If a representative asks to be hired, the Administrator declines and explains this rule.

HR staff classify all aides as W-2 employees at hire. The Administrator may classify a worker as an independent contractor only on written advice of counsel, and the advice is kept on file (see PER-10).

The person who controls pay and employment practices is identified by the governing authority. That person reads the RSA-PCA Guidance Document and submits the OHCQ online RSA Certification form before the license is issued. The confirmation is saved in the Licensure File.

The agency repeats the review and certification whenever OHCQ requires it or when ownership or control of pay and employment practices changes. The Administrator updates the Licensure File within 10 days.
HR staff and the Administrator apply wage, hour and overtime rules in PER-08 to all classified employees, taking account of 29 CFR Part 552 and Maryland law.
The Administrator reviews caregiver level assignments and classification records at the quarterly QA review (see ADM-08).

responsibilities.duty: Determines caregiver level, documents the judgment on adverse consequences, obtains waivers and reassesses at each supervisory visit.
Assigns only workers meeting the required level and never assigns a participant's representative.
Ensures worker classification and the RSA Certification are completed and on file, and obtains counsel's advice before any contractor classification.
Classify aides as W-2 employees and keep classification documents.
Decides whether to sign a waiver of skilled services after the RN explains the risks.

policies.title: Pre-Referral Screening, Criminal History Checks and Employee Registries
policies.applies_to: Administrator, HR staff, supervising RN, and all applicants, employees, independent contractors and contractual employees who provide direct services
policies.purpose: To ensure that no individual is referred to a client until all required pre-referral screening is complete, including criminal history checks, credential verification and employment eligibility. This also ensures that conduct that may be grounds for Board of Nursing action is reported promptly.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] completes the following before referring any employee, independent contractor or contractual employee to a client, as required by COMAR 10.07.05.10: a State or private criminal history check under Health-General Title 19, Subtitle 19; verification of licensure or certification; basic health screening including TB (see PER-05); references; employment history; Form I-9 with identity and employment eligibility verification under 8 CFR 274a.2; an in-person interview; and a skills assessment and demonstration (see PER-04). Criminal history checks are required for all direct service workers, including nurses. Medicaid requires written verification of worker qualifications, and the agency obtains and files it. Screening records are kept in the agency's business office. Conduct that may be grounds for Board of Nursing action is reported immediately to the Board of Nursing and OHCQ. This policy has no separate official checklist item.

definitions.definition: All checks and assessments that must be complete before a worker is first assigned to a client.
A State or private agency background check performed under Health-General Title 19, Subtitle 19 for direct service workers.
Any employee, contractor or contractual employee, including a nurse, who provides hands-on or in-home services to clients.
Verification of a worker's standing on licensing and certification rosters, such as the Maryland Board of Nursing for nurses and CNAs, and the federal OIG exclusion list.

procedures: HR staff open a Screening Checklist for each applicant at the time of application. No worker is scheduled until the Administrator or designee signs the completed checklist.
HR staff complete an in-person interview with the applicant, using a standard question set. The interviewer records the date, interviewer's name and results.

HR staff verify identity and employment eligibility. The employee completes Form I-9 and presents original documents. HR staff examine them and complete the employer section within the time allowed by 8 CFR 274a.2, and file the I-9 as required.

HR staff obtain written authorization and submit the applicant's request for a State or private-agency criminal history records check under Health-General Title 19, Subtitle 19. This applies to all direct service workers, including nurses. No one begins client contact until the result is received and reviewed.

The Administrator personally reviews every criminal history result against the agency's written eligibility criteria and the governing statute, and records a signed decision of eligible or not eligible. Unclear or adverse results are not resolved by HR staff alone. The Administrator decides and documents the reasons.

HR staff verify any required license or certification directly with the issuing source, such as the Maryland Board of Nursing for RN, CNA and CMT credentials. They print or save the verification showing status and expiration date.

As agency practice for Medicaid program integrity, HR staff also check the federal OIG List of Excluded Individuals/Entities before referral and monthly thereafter. A listed individual is not referred or retained.

HR staff obtain at least [NUMBER] references and verify employment history for the prior [NUMBER] years. Each contact is recorded with date, name and summary. Gaps or discrepancies are discussed with the applicant and documented.
HR staff confirm that basic health screening including TB is complete and cleared (see PER-05), and that the RN has documented the skills assessment and demonstration (see PER-04).
HR staff confirm training required by COMAR 10.07.05.11 is complete, and record it in the personnel file (see PER-06).
The agency obtains and files written verification of the worker's qualifications as required by Medicaid, and makes it available for OLTSS and DPICC reviews.

For subcontract agencies, the Administrator requires written evidence that the subcontractor has completed the same screening for its personnel before they are referred. The agency reviews and files that evidence (see PER-10).
The Administrator signs the Screening Checklist only when every element is complete. The scheduler may assign the worker only after the signed checklist is in the file.
Screening records are kept in the agency's business office. Training records go in the personnel file (see PER-07).

If the Administrator or Director of Nursing learns of conduct by a nurse or CNA that may be grounds for Board of Nursing action, the Administrator reports it immediately to the Board of Nursing and OHCQ. The report is made by phone or email the same business day and followed in writing. The worker is removed from client contact pending review.

HR staff re-verify licenses and certifications before each expiration date and check the exclusion list monthly. Any change in criminal history reported by the worker or discovered by the agency goes immediately to the Administrator for review.

responsibilities.duty: Reviews criminal history results, signs screening completion, makes eligibility decisions and reports Board of Nursing conduct to the Board and OHCQ.
Run each screening step, verify credentials, maintain the checklist and monitor expirations and exclusion lists.
Completes and documents skills assessments and clears workers for assignment.

policies.title: Skill Assessments of Employees and Contractors
policies.applies_to: Supervising RN, HR staff, and all employees, independent contractors and contractual employees who provide direct client services
policies.purpose: To ensure that every worker has demonstrated, before the first client assignment, the skills needed to deliver safe personal assistance. The RN verifies those skills, and they are reassessed on a regular schedule and when concerns arise.
policies.policy: This policy meets Application p.5 item B(1)(b)(ii), Personnel - Skill assessments of all employees and contractors, and COMAR 10.07.05.08B(1)(b)(ii). A skills assessment and demonstration are part of the pre-referral screening required by COMAR 10.07.05.10. [AGENCY NAME] completes a skills assessment of each employee, independent contractor and contractual employee before the first client assignment. An RN observes or verifies each personal care skill, and the checklist is signed and dated. Skills are reassessed at the annual review and after any performance concern. Results are kept in the personnel file. The assessment tests the content of training required by COMAR 10.07.05.11, which includes personal care, recognizing situations that need RN referral, record keeping, ethics and confidentiality, CPR, standard precautions, and prevention of abuse and neglect.

definitions.definition: A structured evaluation by the RN of a worker's knowledge and ability to perform the tasks of the role.
Observed performance of tasks by the worker, on a person or in a simulation, with the RN or a qualified designee verifying competence.
A complaint, incident, observation or supervisory finding that raises doubt about a worker's competence or safety.
The agency's standard form listing each skill, the method of verification, the result, and the RN's signature and date.

procedures: The Director of Nursing maintains a Skills Checklist for each role (personal care aide, CNA, CMT, nurse). It lists skills such as bathing, toileting and incontinence care, transfers and positioning, ambulation, dressing, feeding, grooming and skin care, hand hygiene and standard precautions, safe body mechanics, CPR, and recognizing and reporting changes in condition.
HR staff schedule the skills assessment after the worker completes the pre-referral steps in PER-03 and before any client assignment. No client assignment is made without a completed checklist.

The RN observes the worker demonstrating each personal care skill, in a laboratory setting, on a volunteer or by direct observation. Where the RN verifies a skill through documented prior training or certification, the RN also confirms it by direct demonstration or an interview with a documented test of knowledge.

The RN marks each skill as competent or needs training, notes the method and the date, and signs the checklist. A worker with any skill marked needs training receives instruction and supervised practice, and is reassessed before assignment.
CNAs and CMTs are also assessed on the delegated tasks they will perform, and the RN confirms current certification before the assessment (see PER-01 and PC-03).
A worker who cannot demonstrate competence after retraining is not referred. The Administrator documents the decision.

For independent contractors and contractual employees, the RN performs the same assessment. For a subcontract agency, the agency obtains written evidence that its personnel were assessed to equivalent standards and the RN reviews it (see PER-10).
The worker signs the completed checklist to acknowledge the results. The RN and worker each retain the right to add comments.
The RN gives results to HR staff within 2 business days. HR staff file the checklist in the personnel file and update the scheduling system so the worker can be assigned.
The RN reassesses each worker's skills at least annually, at the annual performance review, using the checklist. The date is recorded in the personnel file.

The RN reassesses a worker's skills whenever a performance concern is identified, such as a complaint, incident, supervisory visit finding or change in a client's condition linked to care. The RN decides whether to restrict the worker from client assignments until reassessment is complete.
Skills assessed at supervisory visits (see ADM-10) are noted on the visit record and may serve as an interim reassessment of the observed skills.
The Director of Nursing summarizes assessment results, retraining and pass rates for the quarterly QA review (see ADM-08) and may revise the checklists as needed.
The agency retains skills assessment records in the personnel file in accordance with PER-07.

responsibilities.duty: Performs and signs skills assessments before first assignment, at least annually, and after performance concerns. Decides on restrictions and retraining.
Schedule assessments, file results and ensure no assignment occurs without a completed checklist.
Assigns only workers with a completed skills assessment on file.
Participates in the assessment, completes retraining as directed and signs results.
Ensures resources for assessments and approves decisions not to refer a worker.

policies.title: Health Requirements and TB Screening for Employees and Contractors
policies.applies_to: HR staff, supervising RN, Administrator, and all employees, independent contractors and contractual employees who have client contact
policies.purpose: To protect clients and workers from communicable disease by requiring health screening, including TB screening, before a worker is referred to any client. It also sets out vaccine offers, illness exclusion and confidential handling of health information.
policies.policy: This policy meets Application p.5 item B(1)(b)(iii), Personnel - Health requirements for employees and contractors, and COMAR 10.07.05.08B(1)(b)(iii). Under COMAR 10.07.05.10, [AGENCY NAME] completes a basic health screening including TB before referring any employee, independent contractor or contractual employee to a client. The agency offers hepatitis B vaccine at no cost to workers with occupational exposure, as required by the OSHA bloodborne pathogens standard, 29 CFR 1910.1030. Staff with a communicable illness are excluded from client contact until cleared. Health records are kept apart from the main personnel file and are treated as confidential.

definitions.definition: A health review, performed or reviewed by a licensed health care professional, that confirms the worker has no condition that would pose a risk to clients and includes TB screening.
A symptom review together with a TB test such as a tuberculin skin test or interferon-gamma release assay, performed and interpreted by a licensed health professional.
An illness that can be spread to clients or co-workers, such as active TB, influenza, COVID-19, norovirus, scabies, or infectious skin or respiratory conditions.
Reasonably anticipated contact with blood or other potentially infectious material while performing job duties.

procedures: HR staff give each applicant the Health Screening Form at conditional offer and explain that the screening, including TB, must be complete before referral to any client.

The worker completes the health screening with a licensed health professional. This may be the worker's own provider, a clinic arranged by the agency, or the agency's RN. The professional signs and dates the form to state that the worker is free of conditions posing a risk to clients.

TB screening consists of a symptom review and a TB test. The agency follows current guidance from the CDC and the Maryland Department of Health on test type and follow-up. The worker submits the result with the test date and the signature of the reviewing professional.

A positive test or symptom screen is referred immediately to the worker's health care provider or local health department. The worker does not have client contact until a licensed professional documents that the worker is not infectious. Any treatment plan is followed and documented.

HR staff review all health documents and give them to the Director of Nursing. The RN clears the worker in writing before the worker is referred to a client. The scheduler is informed only that the worker is cleared or not cleared, not the health details.

The agency offers hepatitis B vaccination to every worker with occupational exposure within 10 working days of initial assignment, at no cost. A worker who declines signs the declination statement, and may accept the vaccine later at no cost.

HR staff give each worker the agency's Exposure Control Plan and OSHA bloodborne pathogens training before assignment and annually (see ENV-02 and PER-06). Exposure incidents are handled under ENV-02 and recorded under ENV-09.

Workers report any symptoms of a communicable illness, or exposure to one, to the Director of Nursing before the next scheduled shift. The RN decides if the worker may continue to work, based on current public health guidance.

An excluded worker does not provide client care until the RN receives written clearance from a licensed health professional or the worker meets the exclusion criteria set out by the agency. The Administrator may arrange substitute coverage under PC-07.

If a worker with a communicable illness had client contact, the Director of Nursing assesses exposure risk, notifies affected clients or representatives, and notifies public health authorities where required.

The agency requires TB re-screening and health updates when exposure occurs, symptoms develop, or public health guidance requires them. HR staff track these dates and notify workers 30 days before they are due.

Health records, TB results, vaccination and declination forms, and exposure records are stored in a locked health file, separate from the main personnel file. Only the Administrator, Director of Nursing and HR staff with a need to know have access.
The agency does not disclose a worker's health information to clients, other workers or outside parties except as required by law or authorized in writing by the worker.
The Director of Nursing reports health screening compliance and exclusion events at the quarterly QA review (see ADM-08), without identifying workers by name.

responsibilities.duty: Reviews health screening and TB results, clears workers in writing, decides on illness exclusion and manages exposure follow-up.
Collect and track health documents, offer hepatitis B vaccine, and keep health records in the separate file.
Completes screening, reports illness or exposure promptly and stays off client contact when excluded.
Assigns only cleared workers and arranges coverage when a worker is excluded.
Ensures resources for vaccine and screening and protects confidentiality of health records.

policies.title: Orientation, Competency Evaluation and Annual Training
policies.applies_to: All employees, independent contractors and contractual employees who provide in-home care for [AGENCY NAME], and the RN trainers and supervisors who teach them
policies.purpose: To make sure every caregiver is appropriately trained and has shown competence in the required skills before working alone with a client. Training continues every year, and records are kept in the personnel file.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will not assign any caregiver to a client until the caregiver has completed orientation and initial training and has shown competence in a supervised, documented evaluation. Initial training includes, at a minimum, the content required by COMAR 10.07.05.11 for in-home care: (1) instruction and supervised practice in personal care; (2) recognizing situations that need referral to the RN, including a significant change in client condition; (3) record keeping; (4) ethics and confidentiality; (5) CPR; (6) standard precautions; and (7) prevention of abuse and neglect. The agency adds training on Electronic Visit Verification (ISAS) clock-in and clock-out and on HIPAA privacy and security. Any trainer who is not an agency employee must have OHCQ's written approval before training begins. Training is refreshed at least annually. Every training event is documented in the caregiver's personnel file. Training is part of pre-referral screening under COMAR 10.07.05.10, and the skills assessment and demonstration there is completed before the caregiver is referred to a client.

definitions.definition: The introduction to the agency's policies, client rights, reporting duties, documentation, ISAS and emergency procedures that every caregiver completes before the first assignment.
A documented return demonstration or observation, signed by the RN, showing that the caregiver can safely perform a task.
Any person or organization that is not the agency and provides training required by this policy. OHCQ must approve it in writing first.
A change in the client's physical, mental or functional status, or in the home situation, that may need RN assessment. Caregivers must report it to the RN right away.

procedures: The Administrator designates an RN as Training Coordinator, [RN TRAINING COORDINATOR NAME], who owns the training curriculum and calendar.
Before any training is scheduled, the Training Coordinator confirms the pre-referral screening items in PER-03 are complete, or are scheduled to be finished before the first client assignment.

Orientation covers the agency's mission and organization, the caregiver's job description (PER-01), the scope of services and what caregivers may and may not do (ADM-02), client rights (CR-01), confidentiality (CR-03), grievances (CR-02), incident reporting (ENV-09), emergencies (ENV-05) and workplace safety (ENV-06).

Initial training includes classroom or video instruction plus supervised hands-on practice in personal care: bathing, dressing, grooming, toileting, transfers and positioning, feeding, and mobility assistance.

Training on when to call the RN teaches caregivers to report a significant change in condition, such as a fall, new confusion, skin breakdown, a change in eating, drinking or breathing, a medication problem or a safety concern. Caregivers must call the RN or on-call line the same day, and immediately in an emergency.
Training on record keeping covers accurate, timely, legible entries on the service record or task sheet, and correcting entries with a single line, date and initials.

Training on ethics and confidentiality covers professional boundaries (PER-09), no gifts or financial dealings (CR-04), and HIPAA privacy and security (CR-03). Each caregiver signs a confidentiality statement.
CPR training is provided by a qualified instructor, includes hands-on practice, and is kept current. The certificate and expiration date are placed in the personnel file.
Training on standard precautions covers hand hygiene, gloves and other PPE, safe handling of linens and waste, and cleaning (ENV-02, ENV-03).
Training on abuse and neglect prevention covers recognizing abuse, neglect, involuntary seclusion and exploitation, and the caregiver's duty to report immediately (ENV-08).

ISAS training covers the Medicaid telephonic clock-in and clock-out process, the required use of the client's home phone or approved device, and correcting missed punches (PC-08). Caregivers who will serve Medicaid clients demonstrate it before their first shift.
Before using any outside trainer, the Training Coordinator obtains OHCQ's written approval and files it with the training records.

After instruction, the RN observes each caregiver perform the required personal-care skills on a client or a trained demonstrator. The RN records each skill as competent or not yet competent on the Competency Checklist. A caregiver who is not yet competent receives more training and is re-evaluated before assignment.

The RN signs and dates the Competency Checklist. The caregiver signs the Orientation Acknowledgment. Both go in the personnel file, and the Administrator confirms completion before the Scheduler may assign the caregiver.

The Training Coordinator keeps an annual training calendar. Every caregiver completes annual in-service training that refreshes the required content, plus topics identified through QA (ADM-08), supervisory visits, incidents and complaints.

At least once a year, the RN reviews each caregiver's competency during a supervisory visit or skills check. Any caregiver whose performance shows a gap is retrained, and the retraining is documented.

The Training Coordinator reviews training records quarterly, and 60 days before CPR or other expirations, to identify who is due. A caregiver who is overdue is removed from the schedule until training is complete.

The Training Coordinator files a sign-in sheet, the curriculum or outline, the trainer's name and qualifications, the date and hours, and the OHCQ approval where an outside trainer was used, in each attendee's personnel file.

responsibilities.duty: Makes sure orientation and training are carried out, resources are provided, and no untrained caregiver is scheduled.
Develops the curriculum, teaches or approves trainers, evaluates competency and keeps training records current.
Observes caregiver skills, identifies retraining needs and documents competency.
Assigns only caregivers whose orientation and competency are documented as complete.
Attends required training, performs only tasks in which competency is documented, and asks for help when unsure.

documentation: Orientation Acknowledgment signed by the caregiver
Competency Checklist signed by the RN
Training sign-in sheets, outlines and certificates (including CPR)
OHCQ written approval for any outside trainer
ISAS training completion record
HIPAA training record and confidentiality statement
Annual training log and retraining notes

policies.title: Personnel Records
policies.applies_to: Personnel and screening files for all employees, independent contractors and contractual employees
policies.purpose: To keep complete, accurate and secure personnel and screening records that [AGENCY NAME] can produce for OHCQ at licensure, at renewal and at any inspection, and for Medicaid audits.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a personnel file for every employee, independent contractor and contractual employee. Screening records and personnel records are kept in the agency's business office at [ADDRESS]. Each file holds the pre-referral screening results, current license or certification, health screening including TB, training records, Form I-9, and the skills assessment. The Administrator verifies the current professional licenses and certificates of all employees at license renewal, as COMAR 10.07.05.04 requires. Files are retained for at least six years after the person's last date of service, so the agency can respond to Medicaid audits. Form I-9 retention follows 8 CFR 274a.2. Where the six-year period is longer, the longer period applies.

definitions.definition: The record for one worker containing hiring, screening, qualification, training, health, performance and separation documents.

The documents showing the pre-referral screening items were completed, including criminal history check, license verification, references, employment history, identity and eligibility, interview and skills assessment.

procedures: The Administrator creates a personnel file for each worker at the time of the conditional offer, and the file stays in the business office at [ADDRESS].

The file is divided into sections: application and interview; criminal history and registry checks; license or certification verification; references and employment history; health screening and TB; Form I-9 and identity documents; skills assessment and competency; training; job description and policy acknowledgments; performance and supervision; and separation.
The Administrator keeps Form I-9 and its supporting documents in a separate section or binder so they can be produced for an inspection without exposing the rest of the file.
Training records, including CPR, orientation and annual in-service, are placed in the personnel file by the Training Coordinator within five business days of each training.
Files are kept in a locked cabinet or in an access-controlled electronic system. Only the Administrator, the Director of Nursing and designated HR staff may open them.
Each month, the Administrator audits new files against the Personnel File Checklist to confirm that no item is missing before the worker is assigned.
Before the end of each calendar quarter, the Administrator reviews every file for expiring licenses, certifications, TB screens and CPR, and gives the worker written notice 60 days before expiration.
At license renewal, the Administrator confirms with the primary-source verification that each employee's professional license or certificate is current and places the dated verification in the file.
A worker whose license or certificate has lapsed is removed from the schedule at once until the lapse is cured and documented.
If a worker asks to see his or her file, the Administrator arranges review in the business office within five business days. No document is removed.
Workers sign the Personnel File Acknowledgment confirming they must report changes in name, address, license status, health status and criminal charges to the Administrator.
Files of former workers are retained for at least six years after the last date of service. Records related to a pending audit, complaint, claim or investigation are kept until it is resolved.
After the retention period ends, files are destroyed by shredding or secure electronic deletion. The Administrator records the date and method in the destruction log.
Under the supervision of the Administrator, files are produced to OHCQ, OLTSS, DPICC or other authorized reviewers on request and a record of what was produced is kept.

responsibilities.duty: Owns the personnel files, performs audits, verifies licenses at renewal and approves release of records.
Builds and maintains files, tracks expirations and files documents on time.
Submits training records for filing.
Provides complete documents and reports changes promptly.

documentation: Personnel File Checklist
Form I-9 and supporting documents
License and certification verification records
Expiration tracking log
File audit records
Record release log
Destruction log

policies.title: Wage, Hour, Overtime and Leave Compliance
policies.applies_to: All employees; payroll, scheduling and the Administrator
policies.purpose: To make sure caregivers are paid at least the minimum wage that applies where they work, paid overtime when it is due, given earned sick and safe leave, and covered by workers' compensation, and that required wage reports are filed.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] pays every employee at least the highest minimum wage that applies. The State minimum is $15.00 per hour and Howard County is $16.00. In Montgomery County, from July 1, 2026, the minimum is $16.50 for home care employers with 11 or more employees that receive at least 75% of gross revenue from Medicaid; otherwise it is $18.00 for 51 or more employees, $16.50 for 11 to 50 employees and $15.95 for 10 or fewer. Overtime at one and one-half times the regular rate is paid for hours over 40 in a workweek, consistent with 29 U.S.C. 207. Third-party home care employers do not use the federal companionship exemption (29 CFR 552). Travel time between clients during the workday counts as work time where required. Earned sick and safe leave accrues at one hour for every 30 hours worked, up to 40 hours a year, and is paid leave for employers with 15 or more employees. Workers' compensation coverage is carried for all employees. The agency files the annual personal care aide wage report with the Maryland Department of Labor by September 1.

definitions.definition: A fixed, recurring period of seven consecutive 24-hour periods that the agency uses for overtime.
All time a caregiver is required to work or is permitted to work, including client visits, required training and required travel between clients during the workday.
Leave under the Maryland Healthy Working Families Act that employees earn at one hour per 30 hours worked.
The federal Medicaid access rule's expectation that a stated share of Medicaid payments for personal care goes to direct-care compensation (80% standard from July 9, 2030, per MDH's 2024 report).

procedures: The Administrator sets the pay of each caregiver at or above the highest minimum wage that applies at the caregiver's work location, and rechecks it each January 1 and July 1 and whenever a county rate changes.

Before July 1, 2026, if the agency has caregivers in Montgomery County, the Administrator determines the agency's employee count and share of gross revenue from Medicaid and records which Montgomery rate applies.
The Administrator defines the agency's workweek in writing and communicates it to all employees at hire.

Payroll pays all hours worked, including client visits, orientation and training, required meetings and required travel between clients during the workday. Payroll reviews ISAS and timekeeping records against payroll each pay period.
Employees who report hours worked in excess of ISAS-verified time must explain the difference. Payroll does not ask or allow employees to work off the clock.

Payroll pays overtime at one and one-half times the regular rate for hours over 40 in the workweek. Hours from clients in different programs or counties are added together. The Scheduler reviews weekly schedules each Thursday to flag employees nearing 40 hours.
Overtime must be authorized in advance by the Scheduler or Administrator, but it is paid whether or not it was authorized.
Payroll tracks earned sick and safe leave accrual of one hour per 30 hours worked, up to 40 hours a year, and shows the balance on each pay statement.

The Administrator confirms the agency's employee count each year. At 15 or more employees, leave is paid. Below that, leave is provided as MDOL requires. The Administrator confirms accrual caps and carryover rules with MDOL before finalizing the leave policy.

An employee may use earned leave for the purposes allowed under the law, without retaliation, and a caregiver who needs leave gives notice to the Scheduler as early as practical so client coverage can be arranged (PC-07).
The Administrator maintains workers' compensation insurance covering all employees, keeps the current certificate in the business office, and posts the required notices.
Employees report any work injury to the Administrator immediately. The agency completes the incident report (ENV-09) and the claim forms within the time the insurer requires.

By August 15 each year, the Administrator compiles the personal care aide wage data and files the annual wage report with the Maryland Department of Labor by September 1. A copy of the filing is kept.

The Administrator tracks the 80% direct-care compensation standard that applies from July 9, 2030, reviews the agency's compensation share each year, and reports the result to the governing authority (ADM-01).
Pay records, time records and leave records are kept at least six years (PER-07).

An employee who believes wages or leave were calculated incorrectly may report it to the Administrator, who investigates within 10 business days, corrects any underpayment on the next pay date, and documents the outcome. No employee is retaliated against for raising a concern.

responsibilities.duty: Sets pay, confirms the applicable minimum wage, maintains insurance, and files the annual wage report.
Calculates hours, overtime and leave accurately and reconciles to ISAS.
Plans schedules to limit unplanned overtime and tracks hours.
Reports all hours worked accurately, never works off the clock and reports pay errors.

documentation: Wage schedule showing the applicable minimum wage by county
Timekeeping, ISAS and payroll reconciliation records
Overtime approvals
Leave accrual and usage records
Workers' compensation certificate
Annual PCA wage report filed with the Maryland Department of Labor
Pay error investigations

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
policies.applies_to: All employees, independent contractors and contractual employees
policies.purpose: To protect clients and workers by setting clear standards for ethical conduct, confidentiality and professional boundaries, and to state the consequences of violations.
policies.policy: Caregivers of [AGENCY NAME] treat every client with dignity and respect and keep a professional relationship at all times. Training on ethics and confidentiality is required for all caregivers (PER-06). Caregivers must not accept gifts, loans or tips, enter into any financial transaction with a client, or use a client's property or money for personal purposes. Caregivers must not use a personal phone whose number matches the client's phone number in ISAS verification, and must not clock in or out from anywhere other than the client's home. Clients may accept or reject any caregiver the agency refers without retaliation. Violations lead to discipline up to termination. Suspected abuse, neglect, involuntary seclusion or exploitation is reported under ENV-08.
